comments.note: MovieEditorViewModel.Close() has a defensive guard (if (HasChanges) return) in addition to the CanExecute = HasChangesIsFalse attribute. This is intentional: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm's RelayCommand.Execute does not check CanExecute when called programmatically — the CanExecute is only enforced via UI command binding. The internal guard ensures the contract holds under all call paths (test, UI, and code-behind).

CleanLabelCommand and ShowPropertiesCommand in MovieEditorViewModel.cs are no-op stubs. They will need to be wired in WP-010 and WP-008 respectively, which will modify MovieEditorViewModel.cs to inject ILabelCleanerService and IMoviePropertiesService. The constructor signature will need to grow at that point; consider whether those WPs should add optional nullable parameters or require a constructor change.

The Func<Movie, MovieEditorViewModel> factory registration in Program.cs follows the pattern described in the plan and is consistent with the approach for ShellViewModel's ViewModelFactory delegate. However, this pattern is used only once in the codebase so far — when WP-009 wires MainContentViewModel to use the factory, the convention will be established more broadly.

These fields are correctly reset in the implementation (DiscardChanges restores all 8 editable fields from _originalMovie), but the ResetsAllFields test only validates Label, ActorNames, Studio, and Rating. Low priority since HasChanges=false after discard implies all fields are correctly restored.

Duplicate actor names in ActorNamesText (e.g. 'Alice, Alice, Bob') are not tested. List.IndexOf returns the first match, so the second Alice can never be moved independently. This is an acceptable limitation for the current scope — no requirement addresses this case.
No observations beyond the above — code is clean, well-structured, and consistent with project conventions.

comments.note: Fixed misleading XML doc on the parameterless MovieEditorViewModel constructor. Original text said 'All commands are no-ops in this path' — this is inaccurate because Close, DiscardChanges, MoveActorUp/Down, SetReview, and CancelSetReview all function normally without a repository. Corrected to enumerate only the persistence-requiring commands (ApplyChanges, SaveAndExit, ConfirmSetReview, MarkReviewed, ResetViewCounter) as the ones that are no-ops.

[documentation-forward] IMovieRepository.SaveAsync interface-level doc says 'Persists all editable fields' without clarifying that review, review_message, and watch_count are intentionally excluded. The DapperMovieRepository implementation has a <remarks> tag covering this, but the interface contract itself should state that targeted update operations (SetReviewAsync, ResetViewCountAsync) are the authoritative path for those fields. Add a <remarks> tag to the interface's SaveAsync signature.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md should be updated to include the MovieEditorViewModel public API surface: constructor signatures, all 15 RelayCommands, observable properties, and the CloseRequested event.

[documentation-forward] file-tree.md should be updated to reflect the new files added in WP-006: src/VideoIndexer.App/ViewModels/MovieEditorViewModel.cs and tests/VideoIndexer.App.Tests/MovieEditorViewModelTests.cs. Also record the Func<Movie, MovieEditorViewModel> DI factory pattern in the Program.cs entry.

After ConfirmSetReview / MarkReviewed / ResetViewCounter, _originalMovie is NOT updated with the new NeedsReview / ReviewMessage / ViewCount state. This is correct today because DapperMovieRepository.SaveAsync intentionally excludes those columns. However, it creates a silent correctness dependency: if SaveAsync SQL is ever extended to include those columns, the stale _originalMovie fields would silently overwrite DB state. Consider updating _originalMovie in each targeted command after a successful DB call to make the state self-consistent.

FakeMovieRepository in tests/VideoIndexer.App.Tests/TestHelpers/FakeMovieRepository.cs — the private Throw<T>() helper uses the null-forgiving operator (_exception!) without a null guard. This is safe because all callers check 'if (_exception is not null)' before invoking it, but a defensive null guard or comment would make the intent clearer for future maintainers.

MoveActorDown_IsNoOp_WhenNoActorSelected test case is missing in MovieEditorViewModelTests.cs — the parallel test for MoveActorUp (null SelectedActorName guard) has no counterpart for MoveActorDown. Low risk since both methods share the same null guard pattern, but the asymmetric coverage was flagged by QA. Consider adding the mirror test when the test file is next touched.
